_comment: HOST A EXAMPLE — the owner's four-leg operating profile: ONE codex entry and THREE named Google entries, four legs over TWO families. The codex entry names the recommended explicit codex default, gpt-6-astra / high (spec R-ROSTER, case C35; owner 2026-10-03: one codex leg), so it resolves to four entries over TWO families. Copy this to <source-repo>/.claude/triad-review-legs.json (the project override `prepare --v2` reads from the LIVE checkout, never the round tree) and apply it as a REVIEWED DELTA over whatever that file already holds — do not overwrite unrelated owner configuration. Disabling the shipped `claude` and `google` entries is what makes the round exactly these four entries: the shipped `google` entry would otherwise run BESIDE its three named replacements, and `roster_v2` prints a WARNING for every shipped entry an override moves, at RESOLUTION — on `prepare`'s stdout, before the dispatch lines, not at collect. TWO families is not a defect: a clean round of four valid results folds to AGREED like any other round, and family coverage is reported, never a threshold (R-AGREE); AGREED is the collector's outcome, not a merge authorisation. THE THREE GOOGLE ENTRIES ARE SEPARATE INVOCATION IDENTITIES, NOT PERSONAS: every selected leg receives the same shared purpose, requirements, scope and evidence (R-PROMPT; the owner superseded per-leg review emphases), so the brief carries no per-leg emphasis. `note` is operator prose and never reaches a prompt. HOST A TOPOLOGY: the codex entry is a CLI route (codex_wrapper.py, read-only sandbox) and A's NATIVE family is claude — B's native Codex child is not a template for A. ROUTE: `route` is pinned to agy here because agy is the default Google CLI; where only the older gemini CLI is installed (the compatibility route), pin `"route": "gemini"` instead and move the tier into the `gemini` block — never copy an agy model slug into a gemini control. TIMEOUT 3600 s ON EVERY ENTRY (owner 2026-10-04: a claude or deep-reasoning codex leg can take 30 minutes depending on reasoning; 3600 is twice that). Before it, GOOGLE TIMEOUT 900 s (since 2026-09-26): in round r12 an agy Pro-high / high entry hit the previous 600 s wrapper timeout on a 59 KB gated diff + 26 KB brief (89 tool steps, the vendor turn still in progress; the same-basis retry completed in 434 s) — the wrapper derives its print deadline from --timeout, so the value is the roster DATA that decides it (shared dev log DL-5; a timeout change is a new basis, R-REREVIEW). THREE CONCURRENT GOOGLE CALLS ARE NOT VERIFIED: dispatch these legs SEQUENTIALLY until a real concurrent run is measured. Schema: spec/contracts/review-legs.schema.json (vendored); rules: spec reference/review-rules.md#R-ROSTER.
